title: Elm Hollow retail partner outreach scratchpad
content:
Quick context and hypothesis: Elm Hollow is a mid-size regional retail chain (80 stores, northeast + midwest) that has been experimenting with in-store conversational assistants and the customer service chatbot on their site. They surface long wait times for returns and staff training as core issues; their CX head, Lina Ortega, mentioned interest in reducing transaction-handling time and false-positive fraud flags when customers request refunds. Hypothesis: Redwood can help Elm Hollow reduce per-interaction cost and latency for conversational experiences (in-store kiosks + web chat) by replacing their current multi-model stack with one optimized inference endpoint, enabling offline caching for repeat queries and a fallback routing policy to lighter-weight models during peak events.

What we know (public + quick digs):
- Company size: ~80 stores, ~1200 employees (Glassdoor, LinkedIn org charts show store ops heavy).
- Tech stack hints: using Algolia for search, Intercom for on-site chat, and a mix of GCP and a colocation provider (job postings mention Kubernetes + Terraform). Likely currently using hosted multi-vendor model endpoints (cost pressure mentioned in their 2024 investor Q).
- Decision makers: Lina Ortega (Head of CX) - primary, Tom Warren (Head of Engineering) - technical sign-off, procurement: Dalia Ruiz. Store ops stakeholder: Marcus Hale (Regional Ops Lead).
- Recent signals: job postings for Conversational AI Engineer (Seattle office) and an RFP (internal doc leaked to vendor lists) about “scalable, lower-latency customer chat” posted in Sept 2025.

First outreach sequence (lean PLG + technical hook):
1) Cold email to Lina (short, concrete value prop) — subject: "Reduce wait times for Elm Hollow returns — quick benchmark idea". Mention specific signal: "saw your RFP for scalable chat" and offer a 15-minute benchmark with real latency/cost numbers using a sample of their transcripts.
2) Follow-up note with short technical brief addressed to Tom (cc Lina) — include a one-page sketch of an architecture: Redwood hosted endpoint -> edge caching -> store kiosk fallback; highlight predictable latency, reserved capacity for peak sale days.
3) Internal briefing doc for procurement (Dalia) on compliance: point out Redwood Private (VPC) option, KMS/hardware HSM, audit log features.
4) If we get interest, propose a 30-day pilot: ingest 2K anonymized transcripts, run side-by-side cost + latency comparison vs current stack, present KPIs: median latency, 95p latency, per-1K token cost, error/regression on 10 canonical prompt slices.

Draft cold email (short, audible):
- Subject: "15-min benchmark for Elm Hollow customer chat — concrete latency + cost"
- Body: "Hi Lina — quick note: I saw Elm Hollow’s RFP around scalable chat. We help retailers replace fragmented model stacks with a single predictable inference endpoint that cuts median response time and token costs, while keeping a private deployment option for compliance. Could we run a 15-minute benchmark on a small sample of anonymized transcripts? I can have results (median latency, 95p, and cost per 1k tokens) back in 48 hours. — Asha"

Handling expected objections (rough scripts):
- Objection: "We already have a vendor" -> reply: "Totally — happy to run a non-disruptive benchmark side-by-side. Many teams keep the incumbent but use the benchmark to inform procurement and create pressure during renewal." 
- Objection: "Security / PHI concerns" -> reply: "We support Private deploy and VPC with customer-managed keys and audit logging; we can also run the pilot in a locked-down environment and sign a mutual NDA." 
- Objection: "Migration effort" -> reply: "Pilot requires a small sample and a thin shim for request/response. We provide a connector pattern for Intercom/Algolia flows; full migration is optional and staged."
- Objection: "Cost unknown / vendor lock" -> reply: "We’ll show per-token economics and suggested batching/quantization profiles to match your quality targets; committed Dedicated pools available for predictable billing to avoid surprises."

Pilot success criteria (proposal):
- Latency: median < 250ms for single-turn FAQ queries; 95p < 600ms for multi-turn flows.
- Cost: demonstrable 15–30% unit cost improvement vs current blended stack.
- Quality: no meaningful regression on prioritized prompt set (3% tolerance on key NLU intents).
- Ops: Playbook for fallbacks and runbook for peak events (Black Friday) completed and reviewed by Tom and Marcus Hale.

Tactical notes / next steps:
- Action: Draft short benchmark contract + NDA template (legal), assign to me and Priya for outreach. (Owner: Asha)
- Action: Get a 5k-sample of anonymized transcripts from their help channel (target: 2k for pilot). Ask for CSV export or Intercom dump. (Owner: Marcus)
- Action: Prep a one-pager for procurement that maps Redwood Private features -> Elm Hollow controls (encryption, audit, EULA). (Owner: Priya)
- Internal: Spin up a quick benchmark harness (Jupyter + Redwood API scripted runner) and a dashboard for median/95p latencies. Link: JIRA-3247 (benchmark task).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep messaging concrete: retail examples (returns, POS prompts, store-locator queries) resonate more than generic customer support language.
- Avoid heavy ML-sounding claims in first 2 interactions — focus on latency, cost, and clear compliance options.
- If we get a technical call, bring sample config for autoscaling + reserved Dedicated pool sizing for 80 stores (estimate baseline QPS from transcripts and average session length).

Potential concessions / pricing flex:
- Offer a free initial 48-hour benchmark and a 30-day pilot with a capped bill for the pilot window.
- Consider a 6–9 month discounted reserved capacity for first-year onboarding if they commit to a longer-term SLA.

Meeting prep checklist (if Lina agrees to intro call):
- Quick slide: 3-min value prop tailored to returns/use-case
- Live demo: show 1) median latency comparison, 2) a fallback to a quantized variant under load
- Security slides: VPC + KMS + audit log example
- Ask list: sample size, current vendors, decision timeline, procurement triggers

Open questions / unknowns to research before next outreach:
- Confirm if Elm Hollow’s web chat is routed through Intercom or a homegrown flow.
- Get ballpark monthly active sessions for chat (helps capacity sizing).
- Verify whether refund flows hit their fraud service and if that could be a gating integration.

Personal follow-up plan:
- 2 days after sending first email: follow-up with short technical sketch to Tom.
- 7 days: call attempt via LinkedIn + Slack (if mutual contacts exist).
- 14 days: drop a short pilot proposal and ask for a small commitment (data export + NDA).

Quick win messaging snippets to use in LinkedIn outreach:
- "Elm Hollow — benchmarked latency + cost in 48h, reduced median response time on FAQs by 40% in pilot. Want a fast benchmark?"
- "Retailers: predictable inference for kiosks + web chat w/ private deploy option — we benchmark on your transcripts in 48h."

End of scratchpad. Will iterate after first reply.
